title: Optimize candidate scoring latency with parallel shard execution, token caps, and adaptive deadlines
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency and improve throughput for the /rerank endpoint when scoring variable-sized candidate lists. Scope: server-side changes only (runtime + router + endpoint). Customers: internal benchmarks and high-throughput customers using dedicated capacity. Background: Current implementation processes full candidate lists serially and applies a single global token deadline. This leads to high p99 latency for requests with many long candidates and under-utilized parallelism on multi-GPU hosts. Proposed approach: 1) Candidate shard parallelism - partition the candidate list into N shards (configurable per-model) and execute scoring pipelines in parallel lanes while sharing KV cache and token-level batching inside each lane. 2) Token caps per candidate - enforce a per-candidate prompt/response token limit at router layer to bound worst-case token costs. 3) Adaptive soft deadlines - compute per-shard soft deadlines based on request SLA and number of candidates; allow speculative short-circuiting of low-confidence candidates using an early-exit scorer. 4) Aggressive microbatching + deadline-aware slice sizes - size microbatches per-shard by remaining deadline budget to maximize GPU occupancy without violating tail latency SLOs. 5) KV-prefetch prioritization - prioritise KV cache warmup for shards with longer expected sequences; fall back to prefix caching when prefetch misses. 6) Graceful fallback/hedging - if a shard is slow and approaching deadline, trigger a fallback lightweight model/quantized variant for that shard. Acceptance criteria, rollout, and monitoring are defined below.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for 64-candidate requests reduced from baseline ~380ms to <190ms on dedicated A100 pool (measured over 72h load test)
end-to-end throughput (requests/sec) increases by >=25% for common candidate-size distributions in PLG workload profiles
no regressions in scoring correctness: rank-order correlation (Kendall tau) remains within 0.01 of baseline for the canonical test prompts
token accounting remains accurate and cost per request does not increase more than 5% in steady-state
feature gated rollout available and default-off for Hosted until validation completes
